INFORMATION SECURITY POLICY - REVISION 6
1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This policy sets out the minimum information security controls applicable to
all employees, contractors and third parties who access company systems or
handle company data.
1.2 It applies to all environments, including production, staging, development
and any personal device enrolled in the mobile device management programme.
1.3 Breach of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including
dismissal, and for third parties, termination of the engagement.
2. ACCESS CONTROL
2.1 Access is granted on the principle of least privilege. Each request must be
approved by the data owner and is reviewed quarterly.
2.2 Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all remote access, all
administrative accounts, and any system holding personal data.
2.3 Shared accounts are prohibited except where a documented technical
limitation exists and a compensating control has been approved by the Chief
Information Security Officer.
2.4 Accounts of departing staff must be disabled within four (4) hours of the
termination of employment being confirmed to IT.
3. PASSWORD AND CREDENTIAL STANDARDS
3.1 Passwords must be at least fourteen (14) characters. Complexity rules are
not imposed; length and uniqueness are preferred.
3.2 Credentials must never be transmitted over email, chat or ticketing systems.
The approved secrets manager is the only permitted channel.
3.3 Service account credentials must be rotated at least every one hundred and
eighty (180) days, and immediately on suspicion of compromise.
4. DATA CLASSIFICATION
4.1 All data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted.
Where classification is unclear, data is treated as Confidential until the data
owner determines otherwise.
4.2 Restricted data may not leave approved systems and may not be copied to
removable media under any circumstances.
4.3 Confidential and Restricted data at rest must be encrypted using AES-256 or
an equivalent approved algorithm. Data in transit must use TLS 1.2 or above.
5. INCIDENT RESPONSE
5.1 All suspected security incidents must be reported to the security team
within one (1) hour of discovery, regardless of the hour or day.
5.2 The security team triages every report within two (2) hours and assigns a
severity between 1 and 4.
5.3 A Severity 1 incident triggers the major incident process, including
notification of the executive team within thirty (30) minutes of classification.
5.4 Where an incident involves personal data, the Data Protection Officer
assesses notifiability and, where required, notifies the supervisory authority
within seventy-two (72) hours of the organisation becoming aware.
5.5 A written post-incident review is produced within ten (10) business days for
every Severity 1 and Severity 2 incident.
6. VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT
6.1 Internet-facing systems are scanned weekly. Internal systems are scanned
monthly.
6.2 Critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within seven (7) days, high
within thirty (30) days, medium within ninety (90) days.
7. BUSINESS CONTINUITY
7.1 Backups of all production data are taken daily and retained for thirty-five
(35) days, with a monthly backup retained for thirteen (13) months.
7.2 Restore testing is performed at least quarterly. A restore test that fails
is treated as a Severity 2 incident.
7.3 The recovery time objective for tier-one systems is four (4) hours and the
recovery point objective is fifteen (15) minutes.
8. THIRD PARTY AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT
8.1 Every supplier with access to Confidential or Restricted data must complete
a security assessment before contract signature and annually thereafter.
8.2 Contracts with such suppliers must include a right to audit, a breach
notification obligation of no more than twenty-four (24) hours, and a
requirement to delete or return data on termination.
9. TRAINING AND AWARENESS
9.1 All staff complete security awareness training on joining and annually
thereafter. Completion rates are reported to the audit committee.
9.2 Simulated phishing exercises are run at least six (6) times per year. Staff
failing three exercises in a rolling twelve month period are enrolled in
additional training.
10. POLICY REVIEW
10.1 This policy is reviewed annually, or sooner following a material incident
or a significant change in the regulatory environment.
10.2 Revision 6 was approved by the board on 11 November 2024 and supersedes
Revision 5 in its entirety.

QUARTERLY MARKET BRIEF - UK RETAIL PROPERTY
Prime retail vacancy in the twelve largest UK city centres
edged up to 9.4% in
the third quarter, the first increase in seven quarters. The
rise was
concentrated in secondary pitches, where three national
chains entered
administration during the period and released 41 units
between them. Prime
pitches remained tight, with headline Zone A rents up
2.1% year on year and
incentive packages broadly stable at around 14 months
rent-free on a ten year
term. Investors should treat the headline vacancy figure
with caution: it counts
units marketed for reletting but excludes those held vacant
pending
redevelopment, which we estimate would add a further
180 basis points. The
divergence between prime and secondary has now
persisted for eleven consecutive
quarters and shows no sign of narrowing.
Retail park performance diverged sharply from high street
and should be assessed
separately rather than blended into a single retail figure.
Footfall across
open-format retail parks rose 3.8% against the same
quarter last year, the sixth
consecutive quarterly increase, while high street footfall
fell 1.2%. Rental
growth followed, with retail park headline rents up 5.6%
against 2.1% on prime
high street. The driver is occupier mix rather than
consumer preference: retail
parks have absorbed the discount grocers and
click-and-collect operations that
require parking and servicing high street units cannot
offer. Analysts modelling
retail as a single asset class have consistently understated
retail park
returns, and we expect the gap to widen through the next
two reporting periods.

QUARTERLY MARKET BRIEF - EUROPEAN LOGISTICS
Warehouse vacancy across the six largest European
logistics markets fell to
3.1% in the third quarter, the lowest level recorded since
the series began in
2011. The decline was concentrated in the Netherlands
and the Rhine-Ruhr
corridor, where speculative completions have not kept
pace with take-up for
seven consecutive quarters. Prime headline rents rose
8.4% year on year, and
incentive packages shortened from an average of 9.2
months rent-free to 5.6
months. Investors should note that the vacancy figure
excludes sublet space,
which we estimate adds a further 40 basis points and has
been rising since
March. Occupiers signing before the end of the year are
still securing terms
that will look favourable by the second quarter, but the
window is narrowing
and landlords in the tightest submarkets have begun
withdrawing incentives
entirely rather than renegotiating them downward.
Rail freight volumes tell a different story from the
warehouse market and
should not be read as a leading indicator for it.
Tonne-kilometres across the
continental network fell 2.7% against the same quarter last
year, the fourth
consecutive quarterly decline, driven almost entirely by
bulk commodities
rather than containerised goods. Intermodal volumes were
flat. The divergence
between falling rail tonnage and tightening warehouse
space reflects a shift in
what is being moved rather than how much: lower-value
bulk has migrated to
short-sea shipping while higher-value containerised
freight, which is what
drives warehouse demand, has held steady. Analysts who
treat the rail figure as
a proxy for overall freight activity have consistently
underestimated logistics
property demand for six quarters running, and we expect
that error to persist
through the next reporting cycle unless the reporting
convention changes.

This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into on 14 March 2024
(the "Effective Date") by and between Northwind Analytics Ltd., a company
registered in England and Wales with company number 09488213, having its
registered office at 42 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4AJ ("Supplier"), and
Cedarpoint Financial Group Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal place
of business at 1900 Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103 ("Client").

1.2 "Deliverables" means the reports, dashboards, models and documentation

1.3 "Confidential Information" means any non-public information disclosed by one
party to the other, whether orally, in writing or in any other form, that is
designated as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be
confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of
disclosure.
2. TERM AND RENEWAL
2.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial
term of thirty-six (36) months (the "Initial Term").
2.2 Following the Initial Term, this Agreement shall renew automatically for
successive periods of twelve (12) months each (each a "Renewal Term") unless
either party gives written notice of non-renewal not less than ninety (90) days
before the end of the then-current term.
3. FEES AND PAYMENT
3.1 Client shall pay Supplier an annual subscription fee of USD 480,000, payable
in four equal quarterly instalments of USD 120,000 in advance.
3.2 Supplier may increase the subscription fee once per Renewal Term by no more
than the lesser of (a) four percent (4%) or (b) the increase in the Consumer

3.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Overdue amounts

4.3 Scheduled Maintenance shall not exceed eight (8) hours per calendar month

5.1 Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information in strict
confidence and shall not disclose it to any third party except to its employees,
advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the purposes of this
Agreement.
5.2 The obligations in this Section 5 survive termination of this Agreement for
a period of five (5) years.

6.1 Supplier acts as a processor and Client as a controller in respect of
personal data processed under this Agreement, within the meaning of the UK GDPR.
6.2 Supplier shall not transfer personal data outside the United Kingdom or the
European Economic Area without Client's prior written consent.
6.3 Supplier shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within
seventy-two (72) hours, of becoming aware of any personal data breach.
7. LIABILITY AND FORCE MAJEURE
7.1 Except in respect of death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud,
or breach of Section 5, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or
in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid by Client
in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the
claim.
7.2 Force Majeure. Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in
performing its obligations under this Agreement to the extent that such failure

God, war, terrorism, epidemic, industrial action, or failure of a utility or
telecommunications provider. The affected party shall notify the other party
within ten (10) business days and shall use reasonable endeavours to resume
performance.
7.3 If a Force Majeure event continues for more than sixty (60) consecutive
days, either party may terminate this Agreement on written notice without
liability.

chunks.text: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into on 14 March 2024
(the "Effective Date") by and between Northwind Analytics Ltd., a company
registered in England and Wales with company number 09488213, having its
registered office at 42 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4AJ ("Supplier"), and
Cedarpoint Financial Group Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal place
of business at 1900 Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103 ("Client").
1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Services" means the data analytics and reporting services described in
Schedule A, as amended from time to time by written agreement of the parties.
1.2 "Deliverables" means the reports, dashboards, models and documentation
produced by Supplier in the course of performing the Services.
1.3 "Confidential Information" means any non-public information disclosed by one
party to the other, whether orally, in writing or in any other form, that is
designated as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be
confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of
disclosure.
2. TERM AND RENEWAL
2.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial
term of thirty-six (36) months (the "Initial Term").
2.2 Following the Initial Term, this Agreement shall renew automatically for
successive periods of twelve (12) months each (each a "Renewal Term") unless
either party gives written notice of non-renewal not less than ninety (90) days
before the end of the then-current term.

3. FEES AND PAYMENT
3.1 Client shall pay Supplier an annual subscription fee of USD 480,000, payable
in four equal quarterly instalments of USD 120,000 in advance.
3.2 Supplier may increase the subscription fee once per Renewal Term by no more
than the lesser of (a) four percent (4%) or (b) the increase in the Consumer
Price Index over the preceding twelve months.
3.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Overdue amounts
accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate
permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower.
3.4 Fee schedule by service tier:
  Tier          Included Seats    Annual Fee (USD)    Support Response
  Standard      25                180,000             next business day
  Professional  100               480,000             four hours
  Enterprise    unlimited         960,000             one hour
4. SERVICE LEVELS
4.1 Supplier shall maintain availability of the hosted Services of at least
99.5% measured monthly, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.
4.2 If availability falls below 99.5% in any calendar month, Client is entitled
to a service credit equal to five percent (5%) of the monthly fee for each full
percentage point below the target, capped at thirty percent (30%) of the monthly
fee.
4.3 Scheduled Maintenance shall not exceed eight (8) hours per calendar month
and shall be notified to Client at least five (5) business days in advance.

5. CONFIDENTIALITY
5.1 Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information in strict
confidence and shall not disclose it to any third party except to its employees,
advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the purposes of this
Agreement.
5.2 The obligations in this Section 5 survive termination of this Agreement for
a period of five (5) years.
6. DATA PROTECTION
6.1 Supplier acts as a processor and Client as a controller in respect of
personal data processed under this Agreement, within the meaning of the UK GDPR.
6.2 Supplier shall not transfer personal data outside the United Kingdom or the
European Economic Area without Client's prior written consent.
6.3 Supplier shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within
seventy-two (72) hours, of becoming aware of any personal data breach.
7. LIABILITY AND FORCE MAJEURE
7.1 Except in respect of death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud,
or breach of Section 5, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or
in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid by Client
in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the
claim.
7.2 Force Majeure. Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in
performing its obligations under this Agreement to the extent that such failure
or delay results from an event beyond its reasonable control, including acts of
God, war, terrorism, epidemic, industrial action, or failure of a utility or
telecommunications provider. The affected party shall notify the other party
within ten (10) business days and shall use reasonable endeavours to resume
performance.
7.3 If a Force Majeure event continues for more than sixty (60) consecutive
days, either party may terminate this Agreement on written notice without
liability.

8. TERMINATION
8.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if
the other party commits a material breach that is not remedied within thirty
(30) days of written notice requiring it to be remedied.
8.2 On termination, Supplier shall return or securely destroy all Client data
within sixty (60) days and shall certify such destruction in writing.
9. GOVERNING LAW
9.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the parties
submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
10. NOTICES
10.1 Notices under this Agreement shall be sent to legal@northwind-analytics.example
for Supplier and to contracts@cedarpoint.example for Client, and are deemed
received on the next business day following transmission.
SIGNED for and on behalf of Northwind Analytics Ltd. by Priya Raghunathan,
Chief Operating Officer, on 14 March 2024.
SIGNED for and on behalf of Cedarpoint Financial Group Inc. by Daniel Okonkwo,
General Counsel, on 14 March 2024.
